title: Metabolite Production and Extraction of Indole Compound From Tomato Endophyte Streptomyces sp.
author: Veilumuthu Pattapulavar
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML
materials: Healthy 4-week-old tomato plants grown in natural soil under conditions ( Lycopersicon esculentum ) (Arka Rakshak)
International Streptomyces Project -2 agar (Himedia, CAS number: 8002-48-
Streptomyces DNA Purification kit (Himedia, CAS number: MBA
Mueller Hinton agar (MHA) (Himedia, CAS number: M
Yeast malt agar - ISP2 agar (see Recipes)
Yeast malt agar - ISP2 agar Ingredients Final concentration Peptone 5 g/L Yeast extract 3 g/L Malt extract 3 g/L Dextrose (glucose) 10 g/L Agar 20 g/L
MHA agar Ingredients Final concentration HM infusion solids B # (from 300 g) 2 g/L Acicase 17.5 g/L Starch 1.5 g/L Agar

steps.title: Collect tomato plants
steps.instruction: Gather healthy 4‑week‑old Lycopersicon esculentum plants grown in natural soil (37 ± 2 °C, 12 h light/dark) from the field (coordinates 9.9420° N, 77.9724° E).

steps.title: Surface sterilize stem segments
steps.instruction: Cut stems into 4–5 cm segments with sterile surgical blades and perform the following sequential treatments:

substeps.instruction: Treat with 0.9 % sodium hypochlorite for 4 min.
Rinse thoroughly three times with sterile distilled water.

steps.title: Plate sterilized stems on ISP2 agar
steps.instruction: Cross‑cut the sterilized lower stems, streak onto ISP2 agar (pH 7.2 before autoclaving at 121 °C, 15 psi, 15 min) supplemented with cyclohexamide and nystatin each at 50 µg mL⁻¹ (stock solutions 10 mg mL⁻¹ in ethanol, filter‑sterilized).

steps.title: Incubate plates and subculture
steps.instruction: Incubate plates at 30 °C for 15 days under a light/dark cycle; thereafter perform all work in a laminar‑flow hood. After incubation, pick powdery colonies and subculture onto fresh ISP2 agar plates to obtain pure isolates.

steps.title: Grow broth for DNA extraction
steps.instruction: Inoculate ISP2 broth with the pure isolate and incubate at 30 °C for 7 days with shaking at 120 rpm.

steps.title: Extract genomic DNA
steps.instruction: Extract genomic DNA from the 7‑day broth culture using the CTAB method (Veilumuthu et al., 2022).

steps.title: Quantify DNA
steps.instruction: Measure DNA quality and concentration with a NanoDrop; typical concentration obtained is 146.9 ng µL⁻¹.

steps.title: Prepare sequencing library
steps.instruction: Construct paired‑end libraries with the Illumina TruSeq Nano DNA Library Prep kit and sequence using 2 × 150 bp reads to achieve ~100× coverage.

steps.title: Trim sequencing reads
steps.instruction: Process raw reads with Trimmomatic v0.38 (paired‑end mode) to remove adapters and low‑quality regions using the recommended command‑line parameters.

steps.title: Assemble genome
steps.instruction: Assemble the cleaned reads with SPAdes v3.13.0 using default settings and the ‘careful’ flag to reduce mismatches.

steps.title: Annotate genome
steps.instruction: Run Prokka v1.12 on the assembled contigs for gene prediction, rRNA, tRNA and CDS annotation.

steps.title: Functional annotation
steps.instruction: Perform BlastX searches against the NCBI non‑redundant protein database and map pathways with KEGG KAAS (Automatic Annotation Server).

steps.title: Generate circular genome map
steps.instruction: Create a circular genome visualization using CGView server 1.0.

steps.title: Detect biosynthetic gene clusters
steps.instruction: Run antiSMASH 6.0 on the annotated genome to identify secondary‑metabolite biosynthetic gene clusters.

steps.title: Perform ARTS mining
steps.instruction: Use ARTS for antibiotic‑specific genome mining on the same dataset.

steps.title: Gene ontology analysis
steps.instruction: Annotate GO terms with Blast2GO, retrieve terms via WEGO portal, and categorize them into biological process, molecular function, and cellular component.

steps.title: Produce metabolites in broth
steps.instruction: Inoculate ISP2 broth at a 1:50 ratio with the pure isolate and incubate at 30 °C for 15 days with shaking at 120 rpm; confirm growth by visual inspection of pellets and aggregates.

steps.title: Harvest culture supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the 15‑day broth at 100 × g for 20 min at 4 °C, collect the supernatant and discard the cell pellet.

steps.title: Extract metabolites with ethyl acetate
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of ethyl acetate to the supernatant and shake vigorously for 10 min.

steps.title: Incubate extraction mixture
steps.instruction: Place the flask on a rotary shaker at 200 rpm for 24 h at room temperature (no bead beating required, though it may improve yield).

steps.title: Separate organic phase
steps.instruction: Allow the mixture to stand undisturbed for 30 min, then carefully collect the upper ethyl acetate phase containing the metabolites.

steps.title: Concentrate crude extract
steps.instruction: Evaporate the collected organic phase in a rotary evaporator at 54 °C and 80 rpm until a dry or semi‑solid residue is obtained; collect the residue in sterile glass vials (to avoid plastic interaction) and weigh it.

steps.title: Dissolve and store extract
steps.instruction: Redissolve the dried residue in 200 µL acetonitrile, then store the solution at –20 °C for downstream use.

steps.title: Prepare blank media control
steps.instruction: Process an ISP2 broth without inoculum in parallel as a blank extract to serve as a control during GC‑MS analysis.

steps.title: Perform GC‑MS analysis
steps.instruction: Inject the crude extract into a GC‑MS equipped with a TG‑5MS fused‑silica column (30 m × 0.25 mm × 0.1 µm film). Set electron ionization at 70 eV, helium carrier flow at 1 mL min⁻¹, injector and MS transfer line at 280 °C. Use the temperature program: 50 °C hold 2 min; ramp to 150 °C at 7 °C min⁻¹; ramp to 270 °C at 5 °C min⁻¹; ramp to 310 °C at 3.5 °C min⁻¹.

steps.title: Antimicrobial well‑diffusion assay
steps.instruction: Test the crude extract against E. coli and S. aureus using a well‑diffusion method.

substeps.instruction: Cut 6 mm diameter wells in agar plates with a sterile steel cork borer.

Prepare four concentrations of the extract in ethyl acetate (25, 50, 75, 100 µg mL⁻¹) and add 100 µL to separate wells; include 100 µL ethyl acetate as a negative control and tetracycline as a positive control.
Spread 100 µL of bacterial culture (OD₆₀₀ ≈ 0.6) uniformly over the plate to form a confluent lawn and air‑dry for 10 min.
Incubate the plates at 37 °C for 24 h and measure inhibition zone diameters.
Record results (e.g., indole‑containing extract shows 15–18 mm zones, tetracycline 23–25 mm).
